districts.name: Old Town Triangle
districts.intro: The south-east corner around Crilly Court, Menomonee and Wisconsin streets: a City landmark district of 1870s and 1880s cottages and rowhouses.
districts.work: Kitchen and bath remodels in small, old houses, panel replacements, and exterior work that has to respect landmark rules.

districts.name: Mid-North
districts.intro: Between Armitage and Fullerton, east of Halsted: Victorian rowhouses, greystones and some of the neighbourhood's grandest single-family houses.
districts.work: Whole-house renovations, de-conversions from two or three units to one house, and service upgrades to 200 amps.

districts.name: Park West
districts.intro: The lakefront strip along Lincoln Park West, Lakeview Ave and Pine Grove, up to Diversey: vintage courtyard buildings and high-rises facing the park.
districts.work: Condo unit work under board and management rules: panels, lighting, laundry circuits and EV charging in shared garages.

districts.name: Sheffield and DePaul
districts.intro: Around DePaul University, Fullerton and Sheffield: brick two- and three-flats, student apartments and renovated single-family houses.
districts.work: Service upgrades for multi-unit buildings, meter stacks, basement laundry and outlets, and lighting in renovated flats.

districts.name: RANCH Triangle
districts.intro: Between Racine, Armitage, North Ave, Clybourn and Halsted: 19th-century cottages mixed with newer townhomes.
districts.work: Additions and gut rehabs of frame cottages, new townhome construction, and garage feeds for EV chargers.

districts.name: Clybourn Corridor
districts.intro: Along Clybourn toward the river, including West DePaul: big-box retail, newer townhome developments and the remaining industrial lots.
districts.work: Retail and restaurant fit-outs, new-construction townhomes, and commercial service work.

buildings.title: Greystone two- or three-flat
buildings.where: Mid-North, Sheffield and DePaul, Wrightwood, many with a coach house on the alley
buildings.changes: Services are often still 60 or 100 amps, with a meter for each unit in the basement and a separate house panel for the common areas. Older units may hide knob-and-tube or cloth wiring behind later remodels, and coach houses need their own feed.

buildings.title: Workers' cottage or Victorian frame house
buildings.where: Old Town Triangle, RANCH Triangle and side streets east of Halsted
buildings.changes: Plaster and lath walls, low basements and small original services. In landmark districts, anything visible from the street, like a service mast or meter, may need review. [CONFIRM: which exterior electrical work needs landmark review]

buildings.title: Rowhouse or newer townhome
buildings.where: Old Town Triangle, RANCH Triangle, Clybourn Corridor, West DePaul
buildings.changes: Your own service and panel, roof decks and attached or detached garages. Newer townhomes usually have 200 amps; older rowhouses often don't.

buildings.title: Vintage courtyard building or condo conversion
buildings.where: Park West, along Fullerton, Diversey and Lincoln Park West
buildings.changes: Plaster walls and old conduit or BX cable, unit panels in kitchens or hallways, and condo boards that approve work in risers, basements and common areas.

buildings.title: Lakefront high-rise
buildings.where: Park West, along Lincoln Park West, Lakeview Ave and Diversey
buildings.changes: Concrete slabs limit where boxes can go. Management approval, a certificate of insurance, an elevator booking and set working hours come first.

buildings.title: Shop, restaurant or bar
buildings.where: Lincoln Ave, Halsted, Armitage, Clybourn and Webster
buildings.changes: Older storefronts with apartments above, shared services, signage, and kitchens that need dedicated circuits. Work is scheduled around opening hours.

scope_lede: The same job on paper can cost very differently in a landmark cottage, a greystone two-flat and a lakefront high-rise. These are the things that change it, and most are settled at the walkthrough.
scope_rows: Knob-and-tube, cloth-wrapped cable or old BX in pre-1940 buildings decides whether a circuit can be extended or has to be replaced.
Fishing wire through plaster takes longer, and openings are kept small so patching stays minimal.
Many houses and two-flats still run 60 or 100 amps. Adding an EV charger, central air or an induction range often means a 200-amp upgrade.
Meters, risers and the service mast
Older risers and weatherheads, on the front house and the coach house, have to meet ComEd's rules before a service change.
In Old Town Triangle and Mid-North, exterior changes visible from the street may need Commission on Chicago Landmarks review. [CONFIRM: which exterior electrical work needs review]
Power to a coach house or garage means an underground or overhead feed from the main building.
Vintage condo boards approve work in common areas, risers and basements, often from a written proposal.
Permit parking zones and narrow alleys decide how close the van gets and how long a day takes.
Many jobs go through the City's Express Permit Program. Renovations and de-conversions need plans and a standard review.
Shops and restaurants on Lincoln, Halsted and Armitage often need early or late work. [CONFIRM: whether after-hours rates apply]
hourly_answer: We quote by scope, not by the hour, because the hours on a Lincoln Park job depend on the factors below. Adding a circuit in a gutted townhome and in a plastered 1890s greystone aren't the same job. The written quote tells you the whole price before you agree to it.

honest_context: Lincoln Park is one of our closer neighbourhoods. Our 1,213 Chicago permits are concentrated in Wards 1, 32, 26, 47 and 27, and the 32nd covers the western side of Lincoln Park. Our 49 permits here run steadily from 2013 to 2026, with more of them in the last three years.

Most of Lincoln Park's electrical permits are unit work, lighting, outlets and service upgrades in older buildings, which is our everyday work. Large lakefront high-rise projects go to the big commercial firms.

faq: Can you upgrade the electrical service in my Lincoln Park greystone or two-flat?

Yes. Most move from 60 or 100 amps to 200, which usually means a new meter stack and risers that meet ComEd's rules. We pull the permit and deal with ComEd. Reviewers describe us handling ComEd for a house and its coach house.
Do Lincoln Park's older houses still have knob-and-tube wiring?

Some do, usually hidden behind later remodels. We check at the walkthrough. We don't extend knob-and-tube circuits; where it's still live, we replace the circuits you're touching and tell you what else we found.
Does a landmark district change electrical work in Old Town Triangle or Mid-North?

Inside the house, no. Exterior changes visible from the street, like a new service mast, meter location or exterior lighting, may need review by the Commission on Chicago Landmarks. [CONFIRM: which exterior electrical work needs landmark review.]
Can you run power to a coach house or detached garage?

Yes. We run a feeder from the main building, underground or overhead, sized for what you'll use, including an EV charger. A reviewer had a Tesla charger and a panel upgrade done in one day for a detached garage.
Which Lincoln Park ZIP code do you cover?
All of Lincoln Park, which is mostly 60614, and every other Chicago neighbourhood.
